description.content:
Get the results of a transcription job.
This method takes in the unique ID returned from starting a transcription,
and returns either a JSON (default) or WebVTT response.

If the `Accept` header is missing or of type `application/json` then this call
will return a tuple of status, error, and transcript.
The status will be one of "success", "error", or "pending".
The transcript field will be present if and only if the status is "success".
The error field will be present if and only if the status is "error".
A status of "pending" indicates that the transcription job is still in progress,
in which case neither the transcript nor error will be present.

If the `Accept` header is of type `text/vtt` then this call will return
the transcription as VTT text tracks.

description.content:
Starts a transcription job for a single audio or video file.

The `Content-Type` header in the request must be set to the type of audio or
video being uploaded. The `Content-Type` can be set to any one of the following
mime types that we support:
- `application/mp3`
- `audio/aac`
- `audio/m4a`
- `audio/mp3`
- `audio/mpeg`
- `audio/mpeg3`
- `audio/wav`
- `audio/wave`
- `audio/x-m4a`
- `audio/x-mpeg-3`
- `audio/x-wav`
- `video/mp4`

MP4 video, as a container, can hold any supported audio type.
MP3 and M4A audio support a wide variety of compression and audio codec options.

Files must be less than or equal to 1 gigabyte in size, and the upload must
take less than 30 minutes.

The body of the request can contain a single binary file OR multipart form data.  When
multipart form data is submitted there are a few additional options and requirements:
- The `Content-Type` header of the request must be `multipart/form-data`
- There must be file field with the name `file` which contains the audio / video data,
  the mime type for the data and an optional filename.

description.content:
Starts a transcription request for a single audio or video file.

We support a wide array of audio formats along with their respective compression / codec
options including:
 - AAC
 - FLAC
 - MP1
 - MP3
 - WAV

Currently we only support MP4 video files where the audio streams _must_ be one
of the supported audio formats.

Files must be less than or equal to 1 gigabyte in size, and the upload must
take less than 30 minutes.

Multichannel audio will be merged into a single stream prior to transcription.
In very rare cases this can cause transcription issues with stereo audio when
the two channels have near identical content that is slightly out of phase.

description.content:
Kensho Extract allows users to quickly transform their unstructured documents into a machine-readable format that identifies titles, subtitles, paragraphs, tables, and footers detected within the document in their natural reading order. Kensho Extract interprets messy page layout, structuring text into cohesive paragraphs that can be effectively analyzed and searched.

The Kensho Extract API V3 has incorporated changes to how users must call the API. Please note there are more required fields in API V3 than API V2 (deprecated). The following fields are *mandatory* for `/v3/extractions`: file, document_type, ocr and enhanced_table_extraction.

API V3 introduces new upload and download functionality, allowing the upload of the original document and retrieval of the extracted document output via pre-signed URLs. The pre-signed URLs expire after 15 minutes.
These new endpoints must be called in the following order. - `/v3/extractions/upload-url` - followed by POST'ing the document to the `url` provided in the response - `/v3/extractions/upload-complete` - `/v3/extractions/download-url/{request_id}` - followed by a calling the GET `output_url` provided in the response
